evals.prompt:
This document was written by an engineer who knows the system cold. I need it to read like a textbook chapter that someone with no background in caching or distributed systems could follow from start to finish. They shouldn't be left asking 'wait, what is that?' at any point. Please review it and implement your improvements.

Document: /Users/justin.flammia/.claude/skills/technical-textbook/evals/test-docs/cache-invalidation.md
evals.expected_output: The document should gain: (1) an introduction that explains what cache invalidation is and why it matters before any system specifics, (2) definitions for all acronyms (IP, ISM, KEI, OCSF, GPC, MIP, EVP) before first use, (3) the vague 'GPC and MIP logs, the code reads equivalent provider-specific fields' replaced with actual field names or an honest statement that they aren't covered, (4) step numbering that reflects logical scope (not a single step covering both paths + filtering + flushing), (5) passive voice fixed throughout, (6) no em dashes.

assertions.name: introduces_system_before_mechanics
assertions.description: The revised document explains what cache invalidation is and why it exists before describing any components or steps

assertions.name: no_undefined_acronyms
assertions.description: Every acronym (IP, ISM, KEI, EVP, OCSF, GPC, MIP) is expanded on first use

assertions.name: vague_equivalences_resolved
assertions.description: The phrase 'GPC and MIP logs, the code reads equivalent provider-specific fields' is either expanded with actual field names or explicitly flagged as a gap

assertions.name: no_em_dashes
assertions.description: The output contains no em dashes (—)

assertions.name: passive_voice_reduced
assertions.description: The revised document has meaningfully fewer passive constructions than the original
